dependencies.reason: Builds on Provider, Sandbox, Spec, Capabilities, CheckSpec, SpecError, attach.Dial with its destroy-on-failure and host-side TTL timer, stdioconn, agent.New (for the offline runner seam) and local; this spec adds sandbox.GitRepo, sandbox.ErrNoAgent, attach's GitRepo refusal and the attach.Live accessor.
LocalDir Sync and Export run unchanged over the engine process's stdio, and the integration and smoke tests rely on them.
Uses sandbox.AgentArgs (--ttl, --network, --workdir), Capabilities.Landlock, attach's post-Hello RequireLandlock check and the agent's HOME/TMPDIR Landlock roots that shape the /tmp tmpfs decision.

Uses DefaultImage, OverlayImage, OverlayCopyLine, OverlayImageRepo, AgentPath, the base image layout (uid 1000, /workspace, git), make sandbox-images, and the image harness's engine selection and test variables.
Only the guard package and AllowAll doc comments change, adding the AllowAll guidance that 13 DD 24 deferred; no exported identifier changes.
New's refusal of an unguarded shell tool (checkShellGuard) applies to proxy tools by name and keeps a Guard mandatory for sandboxed runs, which the AllowAll guidance relies on.

tasks.title: Add sandbox.GitRepo, sandbox.ErrNoAgent and the gitclone validation and clone-argv helpers
steps: Write TS-17-1 in sandbox/gitrepo_test.go (package sandbox_test), TS-17-2 to TS-17-5 in sandbox/internal/gitclone/gitclone_test.go and the TS-17-6 property in sandbox/internal/gitclone/gitclone_property_test.go (seeded math/rand/v2 or testing/quick generator, no new module dependency); confirm they fail

In sandbox/errors.go add `var ErrNoAgent = errors.New("sandbox: the image has no executable agent at sandbox.AgentPath")` with a doc comment saying container providers return it, wrapped, after their missing-agent diagnostic

Create package sandbox/internal/gitclone (doc comment: shared by sandbox/podman and the future landlock provider; imports only the standard library and package sandbox, never sandbox/internal/confine)

Implement `Check(repo sandbox.GitRepo) error` for URL: refuse any control byte (< 0x20 or 0x7f) or unicode.IsSpace rune before parsing, then url.Parse; require Scheme == "https", a non-empty Hostname(), User == nil, an empty Fragment and no '#' in the raw string; every message is `gitclone: URL %q: <reason>` so it names the URL field

Extend Check for Ref: empty is fine; refuse a leading '-' or '/', any `..`, and any byte outside ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', '-' and '/', with messages naming Ref; refuse Depth < 0 with a message naming Depth; return nil otherwise

Implement `Args(repo sandbox.GitRepo, dir string) []string` returning `-c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always clone`, then `--depth strconv.Itoa(Depth)` only when Depth > 0, then `--branch Ref` only when Ref != "", then `--`, URL, dir; document that the result follows `git` and that `--` keeps the URL from being read as an option

After validation resolve the binary, then only when Engine is empty run `[<resolved> --version]` once through the runner with a 30-second timeout and parse it; re-check krun against a detected docker; run no other command

tasks.title: Implement Create, the long-lived engine process, the destroy step and Close
steps: Extend sandbox/podman/fake_test.go so the fake's start serves an in-process agent.New(agent.Config{Workdir: t.TempDir(), Env: ...}) over pipes as sandbox/local does, records argv, exits 0 when its stdin closes (or ignores EOF, or exits with a scripted code and stderr), and answers rm/volume rm by script; write TS-17-16, TS-17-22, TS-17-23, TS-17-30 in create_test.go, TS-17-37 to TS-17-39 in destroy_test.go, and TS-17-31 in runner_test.go with a TestMain helper-process fake engine selected by AGENTKIT_FAKE_ENGINE (skipped on Windows); confirm they fail

Add `start(argv, env []string) (process, error)` to the runner seam, where process exposes Stdin io.WriteCloser, Stdout io.ReadCloser, Done() <-chan struct{}, ExitCode() int, StderrTail() string and KillGroup() error

Implement the real start in sandbox/podman/proc.go with os/exec: Env = engine env, stdin from StdinPipe, stdout a private os.Pipe whose write end the parent closes after Start, stderr drained by a goroutine into a tail buffer keeping the last 8 KiB, and a Wait goroutine recording the exit code and closing Done; proc_unix.go sets SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true} and kills with syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL); proc_windows.go makes both no-ops (Process.Kill fallback)
Add `shortOptions(env)` returning tools.ExecOptions{Env: env, Timeout: 2 * time.Minute, MaxBytes: a bounded tail} and route every short engine command through it

Replace the temporary Create in sandbox/podman/create.go: `eff, err := sandbox.CheckSpec(p.Capabilities(), spec)` returned unchanged; if eff.Image is empty set it from p.defaultImage(), returning its error (wrapping ErrNoPublishedImage) unchanged before any command; then id = 16 lowercase hex from crypto/rand and created = p.now()

Run `volume create <labelArgs...> agentkit-<id>` (on failure return an error with the output tail and run nothing else), then start the engine process with [bin] + Args(p.opts with resolved Engine, id, created, eff); if start fails run the destroy actions directly and return the joined error

Implement the destroy step in sandbox/podman/destroy.go as a closure that captures no Create ctx: wait up to 5 s on Done, else KillGroup and wait briefly; then run `rm -f agentkit-<id>`, `rm -f agentkit-<id>-init`, `volume rm agentkit-<id>`, each regardless of earlier failures, joining errors with errors.Join

Treat "no such container"/"no such volume" (case-insensitive "no such") output as success; when volume rm reports the volume in use ("is being used", "in use") retry every 500 ms until 10 s have passed, then return an error naming agentkit-<id>; keep the whole step inside attach's 30-second budget

Call attach.Dial(ctx, stdioconn.New(proc.Stdout, proc.Stdin), attach.Config{ID: id, Spec: eff, Destroy: destroy, Provider: engine name}); on failure return the Dial error with the stderr tail appended (task 6 refines the classification); on success return the provider's wrapper type in sandbox/podman/sandbox.go that holds the attached sandbox, id, created and eff and forwards every method (Close stays idempotent through attach)

Confirm the recorded run argv carries --rm and AgentArgs' --ttl and the volume create argv carries the expires label (two-sided TTL), and that TS-17-22's hook changes Sandbox.Spec().Image to the default image
Run `cd sandbox && go test ./podman/` and `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` in sandbox/ until green

tasks.title: Classify Create failures, diagnose a missing agent, and leave nothing behind
steps: Extend the fake so the engine process can serve a fake agent reporting ProtocolMajor 99 (sandbox/internal/fakeagent or a minimal sandboxpb server), an agent.New with Landlock ABI 0, a process that never answers Hello, scripted exit codes and stderr, and scripted diagnostic answers; write TS-17-32 to TS-17-36 in create_fail_test.go and TS-17-40, TS-17-41 in ttl_test.go; confirm they fail

In create.go classify a Dial failure in this order: errors.Is(err, sandbox.ErrProtocol) or errors.As to a *sandbox.SpecError with Field RequireLandlock returns the error unchanged; a done ctx returns fmt.Errorf("podman: create: %w", ctx.Err()) with the Dial error in the message

Otherwise wait for the process's Done (attach's destroy has already waited or killed it) and read ExitCode(); 125 returns an error naming the engine and exit status 125 with the stderr tail and runs no diagnostic

Any other diagnostic result returns an error wrapping the Dial (handshake) error with the original engine stderr tail

Audit every failure path after volume create (start failure, 125, diagnostic 127, diagnostic 0, protocol 99, ctx cancelled during Hello) so each runs rm -f agentkit-<id>, rm -f agentkit-<id>-init and volume rm agentkit-<id> exactly once, and a failing volume create runs neither run nor volume rm

Confirm the host-side TTL path: attach's timer calls teardown, which runs the provider's destroy closure from the timer goroutine, and that no provider goroutine removes the volume when the engine process ends early (it stays until Close, the TTL or Reap)
Run `cd sandbox && go test ./podman/` until green

tasks.title: Sync a GitRepo through the init container under the GitRepo slot rules
steps: Extend the fake so the init command (argv containing `--entrypoint git`) can write files into the fake agent's workdir, block until released or until its ctx is done, fail to start, or exit with a scripted status and output, recording its ctx deadline; give the fake agent's Env a PATH holding a stub git (or none); write TS-17-42 to TS-17-46, TS-17-48 and TS-17-49 in sandbox/podman/gitrepo_test.go; confirm they fail
In sandbox/podman/sandbox.go give the wrapper a sync.RWMutex and an atomic slotTaken flag; ID, Spec, Agent, Export and Close forward to the attached sandbox

Tools takes the read lock for the call, sets slotTaken whatever the outcome, and forwards; Sync of any non-GitRepo source takes the read lock for the call, forwards, and sets slotTaken only on success

In sandbox/podman/gitrepo.go implement the GitRepo branch holding the write lock for its whole duration (so it waits for in-flight Tools/Sync and holds new ones): first attach.Live(inner), then gitclone.Check(repo), then the slot rule returning `podman: GitRepo must be the first Sync and come before Tools`, then Agent().Git false returning `podman: the image needs git on its PATH for a GitRepo`; none runs a command and none takes the slot

Run [bin] + InitArgs(p.opts, id, created, eff, repo) through the runner with a context from context.WithDeadline(ctx, created.Add(eff.TTL)) and a timeout no later than that expiry, using the wrapper's stored eff (Workdir /workspace), not the attached Spec()
Exit 0 sets slotTaken and returns sandbox.SyncResult{} and nil; document on Sync that a GitRepo reports zeros and that the clone's files are visible to the tools
Exit 126 or 127 returns an error saying the image cannot run git; any other non-zero exit returns an error naming the URL and carrying the output tail; neither takes the slot

A start error, a cancelled ctx or the expiry (ctx.Err() set or Outcome timeout/abort) runs `rm -f agentkit-<id>-init` under context.WithoutCancel(ctx) and the short-command timeout before returning an error wrapping ctx.Err(); the slot stays free
Run `cd sandbox && go test -race ./podman/` until green
